description: FLAM is a multi-tenant SaaS platform for Kenyan public transit (matatu) operators, SACCOs, drivers, and passengers. It combines real-time GPS fleet tracking, Hyperledger Fabric compliance ledger, M-Pesa-native payments, route analytics, and role-based dashboards to digitize and monetize the informal transit ecosystem.

evidence: Presence of MapLibre, GPS ping ingestion, and route analytics strongly indicates a fleet/transit management platform
Hyperledger Fabric integration signals compliance-grade audit trail requirements typical of regulated transport sectors
M-Pesa STK Push as primary payment method targets Kenyan market; SACCO and matatu terminology confirms public transit vertical
Role types include REGULATOR, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, PLANNER, CREW, OPERATOR, and PASSENGER — matching a multi-stakeholder transit ecosystem
Revenue config with reservation fees, daily collections, and driver tips maps directly to matatu fare collection workflows
NTSA compliance references and route-level congestion scoring confirm government-regulated public transit context

current_growth_features.detected_intent: Facilitates user onboarding by routing new users to role-specific dashboards based on declared intent (passenger, crew, operator, owner, org). This branching point determines which growth loop a new user enters and is the foundation of all role-based activation flows.
growth_potential: Add PostHog capture on intent selection to measure which roles are most commonly chosen and where drop-off occurs
Implement a guided onboarding checklist per intent type (e.g. operator checklist: add vehicle → pair GPS tracker → add driver → view dashboard)
Add progress persistence so users who abandon mid-onboarding can resume where they left off
A/B test intent label copy — 'operator' vs 'fleet manager' may resonate differently with target users
Add an 'I'm not sure' path that asks qualifying questions and recommends an intent, reducing wrong-role registrations
Track intent-to-activation rate: what % of users who select 'operator' actually complete their first GPS ping

growth_potential: Implement dunning sequence for failed STK pushes: immediate in-UI retry prompt, Upstash Redis delayed SMS at day 1, Resend email with manual payment link at day 3, with a 3-day grace period before downgrade
Add annual plan variants at 20% discount to increase LTV and reduce involuntary churn from monthly renewal failures
Surface the isExpiringSoon flag as a persistent banner in the org dashboard (not just billing page) to create renewal urgency earlier
Add a seat-count selection step before Business plan checkout to correctly calculate per-user pricing
Implement Upstash Redis job to send SMS renewal reminder 3 days before plan expiry
Track STK push abandonment rate in PostHog (pending → failed vs pending → completed) to measure payment friction

growth_potential: Audit all routes calling Stripe helpers and either fully migrate to M-Pesa or explicitly route international/card users through Stripe with clear branching logic

Remove the Stripe test card FAQ entry from the pricing page to eliminate trust-eroding inconsistency
If fully migrating to M-Pesa, remove Stripe SDK dependency to reduce bundle size and eliminate confusion for future developers

growth_opportunities.description: The majority of Kenyan matatu operators are mobile-first users who communicate primarily via WhatsApp. There is currently no WhatsApp-based onboarding path — all registration requires navigating a web form. Building a WhatsApp Business API flow (using Firebase Cloud Messaging or a WhatsApp BSP) that guides operators through profile creation, SACCO selection, and vehicle registration via conversational messages would dramatically reduce onboarding friction. The flow would emit the same PostHog events and Supabase inserts as the web path, making it a parallel channel rather than a replacement. This directly extends the existing GPS flywheel by removing the web-form barrier that prevents operators from reaching their first GPS ping.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Contextual In-App Feature Gate Component with Upgrade Modal
growth_opportunities.description: Free tier limits (vehicles, geofences, route alerts, seats) exist only as marketing copy — there is no enforcement or contextual upgrade prompt anywhere in the codebase. A reusable Svelte FeatureGate component should wrap any action that exceeds tier limits and render an upgrade modal with: (1) the specific limit hit, (2) what the next tier unlocks, (3) a one-tap M-Pesa STK push CTA. This is the single highest-leverage free-to-paid conversion mechanism in product-led growth and is entirely absent. It is complementary to the existing GPS flywheel (which focuses on Day-28 compliance gate) by capturing upgrade intent at the moment of value realization across all features, not just GPS history depth.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: SACCO-to-SACCO Referral Program with WhatsApp Share
growth_opportunities.description: The matatu SACCO ecosystem is a tight-knit, trust-based network where word-of-mouth from a respected ORG_CHAIR carries more weight than any marketing channel. There is currently no referral mechanism. Building a referral program where ORG_CHAIRs earn one month free on their current plan for each referred SACCO that completes its first M-Pesa subscription payment would create a viral acquisition loop native to the market. The referral link should be shareable directly via WhatsApp from the org dashboard, and the funnel tracked end-to-end in PostHog. This is entirely distinct from the GPS broadcast flywheel and addresses top-of-funnel acquisition rather than activation and retention.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Passenger Trip Score Sharing & WhatsApp Viral Loop
growth_opportunities.description: The tripScore store already computes a 0-100 commute quality score per trip but it is never surfaced to passengers in a shareable format. Adding a post-trip summary card with the trip score, route name, and a pre-composed WhatsApp share message ('My Nairobi CBD → Westlands commute scored 91/100 on FLAM — book smarter matatus') would create a zero-cost viral acquisition channel. Each share exposes the platform to the sharer's WhatsApp contacts (typically dozens of commuters on the same routes). This is a complementary passenger-side growth loop entirely separate from the operator-focused GPS broadcast flywheel, targeting a different user segment and growth motion.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Operator Activation Checklist with Progress Persistence
growth_opportunities.description: New operators currently have no guided path from account creation to first GPS ping. There is no checklist, no progress indicator, and no persistence if they abandon mid-onboarding. A role-specific activation checklist (Add vehicle → Pair GPS tracker → Add driver → View first trip → Enable compliance alerts) stored in Supabase and surfaced prominently in the operator dashboard would dramatically reduce the time-to-first-GPS-ping metric that the GPS flywheel depends on. Progress should persist across sessions and resume automatically on re-login. Incomplete checklist steps should trigger Upstash Redis delayed SMS nudges at Hour-24 and Day-3. This extends and accelerates the existing GPS flywheel without duplicating it.

ORG_CHAIRs currently must log in to see KPI trends. There is no automated outbound engagement that brings them back to the platform. A weekly Resend email digest delivering top-line metrics (total fleet revenue, on-time %, top-performing route, vehicles with compliance alerts, week-over-week change) with deep links to the relevant dashboard sections would drive re-engagement without requiring login. The Resend infrastructure is already in the stack. This is a retention mechanism for the operator segment that is orthogonal to the GPS ping flywheel — it targets already-activated operators and reinforces the value of maintaining their paid subscription by making platform value visible in their inbox.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Compliance PDF/CSV Export for NTSA Submissions
growth_opportunities.description: SACCO operators are legally required to submit compliance reports to NTSA (Kenya's transport regulator). The platform already captures rich compliance event data (severity, timestamps, resolution status, vehicle IDs) but offers no export capability. A one-click PDF or CSV export of compliance events, formatted to match NTSA submission requirements, would be a high-value retention feature that makes the platform operationally indispensable. Gating this export behind Pro+ tier creates a clear, compliance-driven upgrade incentive. This is a distinct retention mechanism from the GPS ledger compliance gate — it targets the reporting workflow rather than the GPS history depth narrative.

The M-Pesa B2C payout infrastructure (sendB2CPayment) and an 80% platform tip share are already configured in the revenue engine, but there is no in-app tipping UI anywhere in the passenger-facing flow. Building a post-trip tipping screen with quick-select amounts (KES 20, 50, 100) triggered after a reservation is marked complete would activate an entirely dormant revenue stream. Even 10% tip adoption at an average KES 40 tip would meaningfully increase platform revenue. This is a net-new monetization surface that does not overlap with subscription billing or the GPS flywheel.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Passenger Booking Streak & Loyalty Badge System
growth_opportunities.description: Passenger retention is currently driven only by route quality (tripScore) with no explicit loyalty mechanism. A streak system — where passengers who book via the app for 5 consecutive weekdays earn a visible loyalty badge on their profile, and 20-trip milestones unlock a small M-Pesa cashback credit — would create habitual return behavior. Streaks reset on missed days, creating loss-aversion that drives daily opens. Badge visibility on the passenger profile creates social proof for the platform. This is a passenger-segment retention loop entirely separate from the operator-focused GPS flywheel.

ORG_CHAIRs currently see their own KPIs in isolation with no external reference point. Adding a SACCO Health Score (0-100, derived from GPS ping frequency, fleet uptime, compliance event resolution rate, and revenue collection consistency) alongside anonymized percentile benchmarks ('Your fleet is in the top 30% of SACCOs on this platform') creates social comparison motivation and makes improvement visible. Benchmarks also serve as a subtle upgrade nudge — top-quartile metrics are only achievable with Pro-tier features like advanced analytics and route optimization. This is a retention and expansion feature distinct from the GPS flywheel's compliance framing.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Anonymized Transit Data API for Urban Planners & Regulators
growth_opportunities.description: The platform accumulates uniquely valuable anonymized GPS traces, passenger volume patterns, route adherence data, and compliance event distributions that urban planners, government regulators (NTSA, county governments), and transport researchers would pay for. A 'Transit Data API' subscription product targeting PLANNER and REGULATOR roles at KES 20,000-50,000/month would create a high-margin B2G revenue stream with near-zero marginal cost, leveraging DuckDB (already in stack) for aggregation. This is a net-new revenue segment (B2G) that does not compete with or overlap with the operator SaaS subscription model.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: 14-Day Pro Trial with Time-Gated Downgrade Warning
growth_opportunities.description: New signups can currently remain on the free tier indefinitely with no time pressure or urgency to convert. A 14-day Pro trial automatically activated on account creation — with a countdown banner in the dashboard, Resend email nudges at day 7 and day 12, and a final 'Your Pro trial ends tomorrow' SMS on day 13 — would expose all operators to the full platform value before the conversion decision. The trial should use the existing plan state management in the M-Pesa payments store and require no new infrastructure. This is a top-of-funnel conversion mechanism that complements the GPS flywheel's Day-28 compliance gate by creating an earlier, broader conversion opportunity.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Admin Activation SLA Dashboard & Alert System
growth_opportunities.description: Operator activation latency (time from org creation to admin approval) is a direct churn trigger — operators who wait more than 24 hours for activation have significantly higher abandonment rates. There is currently no visibility into this metric for the admin team. An internal admin dashboard widget showing median activation time, queue depth, and SLA breach alerts (orgs waiting >12 hours) with an automated Resend email to the admin team when queue depth exceeds 5 would reduce activation latency and recover operators who would otherwise churn before experiencing the platform. This is an operational efficiency feature that accelerates the top of the GPS flywheel funnel.

The network analytics dashboard already computes real-time congestion scores per route, but this data is only accessible to users who actively log in and navigate to the analytics tab. A configurable SMS alert subscription — where operators and passengers can set a congestion threshold per route and receive an SMS when it is exceeded — would create a daily active use driver that operates entirely outside the app. Using Upstash Redis delayed jobs and the existing SMS infrastructure, this feature would drive habitual re-engagement for both operator and passenger segments. Gating threshold configuration (e.g., more than 2 monitored routes) behind Starter+ tier creates a clear upgrade incentive.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: Compliance Module Add-On for Regulators & Compliance Officers
growth_opportunities.description: REGULATOR, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, and PLANNER roles have dedicated dashboard surfaces but are lumped into the same pricing tiers as operators, with no role-specific value proposition or pricing. A 'Compliance Module' add-on at KES 5,000-15,000/month targeting these institutional roles would package: NTSA-formatted compliance report exports, multi-org fleet oversight views, audit trail downloads from the Hyperledger Fabric ledger, and anomaly detection alerts. These roles work within organizations with procurement budgets and are willing to pay for specialized tooling. This opens a B2G revenue segment entirely separate from the operator SaaS model.

growth_opportunities.feature_name: In-App Operator Community Feed & Route Announcements
growth_opportunities.description: Matatu operators and SACCO managers currently have no platform-native communication channel — coordination happens via WhatsApp groups outside the platform, reducing stickiness. A lightweight community feed within the org dashboard — where ORG_CHAIRs can post route announcements, schedule changes, and compliance reminders visible to all org members — would increase daily active use and embed the platform into existing operational workflows. Push notifications via Firebase (already in stack) would drive re-engagement. This is a community/engagement feature with no overlap with the GPS broadcast or compliance flywheel.

revenue_leakage.issue: Fleet Manager feature available on Free tier with up to 5 vehicles — a core operational feature given away for free that should drive paid upgrades
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Limit Free tier Fleet Manager to 1-2 vehicles maximum, or remove it entirely from Free and make it a Starter+ feature. Fleet management is the primary value proposition for OWNER/VEHICLE_OWNER segments who will pay for it — giving it away on Free removes the main upgrade incentive.

revenue_leakage.issue: Insights Snapshot analytics is available on the Free tier with no restrictions — analytics is a strong paid conversion driver and should not be freely available without meaningful limits
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Remove Insights Snapshot from Free or severely restrict it (e.g., last 7 days only, no drill-down, no export). Analytics is a key value proposition for operators — restricting it creates a clear upgrade path to Starter/Pro.

revenue_leakage.issue: Annual billing toggle in pricing_module.svelte is broken — getDisplayPrice() and getDisplayInterval() reference plan.stripe_price_id which does not exist on the PricingPlan interface, causing the annual discount calculation to silently fail. The 'Save 20%' chip appears but no prices change.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Fix the annual billing toggle to use the correct field (mpesaAmount or a new annual_mpesa_amount field). The 20% annual discount is a strong conversion and retention lever — users who commit to annual plans have significantly lower churn. Add annual plan variants with correct KES amounts to pricing_plans.ts.

revenue_leakage.issue: No annual subscription option implemented in the M-Pesa payment flow — only monthly plans exist, missing significant LTV and retention opportunity despite the UI advertising a 20% annual discount
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Add annual plan variants (starter_annual, pro_annual, business_annual) with 20% discount as advertised. Annual plans improve cash flow, reduce involuntary churn from monthly renewal failures, and increase LTV. Wire them into the M-Pesa STK push flow with correct lump-sum KES amounts.

revenue_leakage.issue: No in-app feature gates or upgrade prompts — users who hit free tier limits (3 route alerts, 5 geofences, 1 seat, 5 vehicles) receive no contextual upgrade prompt. Free tier limits exist only as marketing copy with no enforcement or conversion mechanism anywhere in the codebase.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement server-side enforcement of tier limits and build a reusable FeatureGate Svelte component that triggers upgrade modals when free users attempt to exceed limits. Show upgrade CTAs contextually (e.g., 'You have used 3/3 Route Alerts — upgrade to Starter for 25') rather than only on the billing page. This is the highest-leverage free-to-paid conversion mechanism in PLG.

revenue_leakage.issue: Free tier vehicle limit has no enforcement in code — pricing plan lists '5 vehicles' but there is no enforcement mechanism visible in the codebase, meaning free users can potentially add unlimited vehicles without upgrading
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement server-side enforcement of vehicle limits per subscription tier. Add a check in vehicle creation endpoints that queries the user's current plan and vehicle count before allowing inserts. Without enforcement, free tier limits are marketing copy only and users have no reason to upgrade.

revenue_leakage.issue: Business plan at KES 4,900/user/month is priced per user but the M-Pesa STK push sends a single fixed amount of KES 4,900 regardless of team size — causing severe revenue leakage for any multi-user Business plan customer
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a seat-count selection step before Business plan checkout that calculates total = KES 4,900 × seats with volume discount tiers applied (KES 3,900 at 10+, KES 2,900 at 50+). The current flow charges a flat KES 4,900 regardless of team size, causing severe revenue leakage for multi-seat customers.

revenue_leakage.issue: KES 19 reservation fee may not cover M-Pesa transaction costs — at this price point the platform share (KES 15) risks being negative-margin after M-Pesa fees, especially for single-seat bookings
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Review the KES 19 reservation fee against M-Pesa transaction costs (typically KES 0-33 depending on amount tier). Consider raising the fee to KES 25-30 to ensure positive margin, or implement a minimum booking value. Consider a percentage-based fee model tied to fare value rather than a flat fee to scale revenue with transaction size.

revenue_leakage.issue: Stripe integration code still actively imported and used (subscription_helpers.server.ts with full Stripe SDK) while M-Pesa is the active payment processor — dead code suggests incomplete migration and potential for confused payment paths resulting in uncharged users
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Audit whether any routes still call Stripe subscription helpers. If fully migrated to M-Pesa, remove Stripe code to eliminate confusion and potential accidental routing failures. If Stripe is needed for card-paying or international users, make it an explicit secondary payment method with clear routing logic and ensure both paths are tested end-to-end.

revenue_leakage.issue: FAQ on the pricing page references Stripe test cards ('Use Stripe test card 4242...') despite the platform being M-Pesa only — creates confusion and signals an incomplete product to potential customers, reducing conversion trust
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Update the FAQ to remove all Stripe references and replace with M-Pesa sandbox or testing instructions. Outdated payment copy erodes trust and may cause potential customers to abandon the signup flow when they see mismatched payment method references.

revenue_leakage.issue: No trial period or freemium-to-paid conversion mechanism — users can stay on the free tier indefinitely with no time pressure, trial expiry, or urgency nudging them toward paid plans
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a 14-day Pro trial for new signups to let users experience premium features before reverting to Free. Add time-based upgrade prompts (e.g., 'Your Pro trial ends in 3 days') and email sequences via Resend targeting free users who have used the product but not converted after 7, 12, and 14 days.

revenue_leakage.issue: Billing page shows no upsell path for active subscribers on lower tiers — a Starter subscriber sees no 'Upgrade to Pro' option, missing cross-sell and upgrade revenue from existing paying customers
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Show a plan comparison and upgrade CTA for active subscribers on lower tiers. Add a 'Change Plan' button that shows the full pricing module with current plan highlighted and a clear value proposition for upgrading. Existing paying customers are the highest-conversion upgrade audience.

revenue_leakage.issue: No payment failure recovery flow — when an M-Pesa STK push fails on subscription renewal, there is no automated retry logic, SMS or email dunning sequence, or grace period before downgrade. Involuntary churn from payment failures is entirely unrecovered.
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a 3-step dunning flow: (1) immediate retry prompt in UI when STK push fails, (2) SMS reminder at day 1 via Upstash Redis delayed job, (3) email with manual payment link at day 3 via Resend, with a 3-day grace period before downgrading to Free. The Upstash Redis and Resend infrastructure is already in the stack.

revenue_leakage.issue: API Access is gated behind Pro+ plans but there is no API usage metering, rate limiting enforcement, or API add-on product — enterprise API consumers have no way to pay for higher quotas and overages go entirely unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Define and enforce API rate limits per tier (e.g., 1,000 calls/day on Pro, 10,000 on Business, unlimited on Enterprise). Offer an API add-on pack for Pro users who need more calls. API metering creates a natural usage-based revenue stream and upgrade trigger for high-volume users.

revenue_leakage.issue: Multiple high-value roles (REGULATOR, PLANNER, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, ACCOUNTANT) have dedicated dashboards but no differentiated pricing — the entire B2G and institutional buyer segment is completely unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Create role-specific pricing or add-on modules for regulatory and compliance features. These users have specialized, high-value needs and work within organizations with procurement budgets. A 'Compliance Module' add-on at KES 5,000-15,000/month targeting REGULATOR and COMPLIANCE_OFFICER roles could capture significant B2G revenue.

revenue_leakage.issue: Tips are configured at 80% platform share in revenue-config.ts but there is no in-app tipping UI in any passenger-facing flow — this revenue stream exists in the backend but is entirely unsurfaced to users, leaving it effectively inactive
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Build a prominent post-trip tipping screen in the passenger booking flow with suggested tip amounts (KES 20, 50, 100) as quick-select options triggered after a reservation is marked complete via M-Pesa STK push. Even 10% tip adoption at average KES 40 per tipping transaction would meaningfully increase platform revenue given the 80% platform share.

revenue_leakage.issue: No usage tracking or usage-based billing — the platform collects rich telemetry (trips, bookings, geofences, route alerts) but does not monetize usage overages, meaning power users on free or low tiers receive unlimited value without paying for it
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Consider adding usage-based add-ons (e.g., pay-per-booking above plan limits, additional geofence packs at KES 200/10 geofences, extra route alert bundles at KES 100/10). This captures revenue from power users who exceed limits rather than losing them to free tier abuse or churn.

revenue_leakage.issue: The /billing/manage route silently redirects to /account/billing with no functionality — users expecting a billing portal with invoice downloads, payment method management, and renewal history find nothing, reducing perceived value of paid plans
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Build out the billing management page with: (1) downloadable payment receipts and invoices, (2) subscription renewal date and auto-renewal toggle, (3) plan change history. A professional billing experience increases trust, reduces support tickets, and reduces churn among paying customers who judge product quality by operational polish.

revenue_leakage.issue: No referral or affiliate program — the platform serves a tight-knit network-effect market (matatu operators, SACCOs, drivers) where word-of-mouth is the dominant acquisition channel, but organic referrals are not captured or incentivized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Implement a referral program where existing operators earn KES billing credits (e.g., 1 month free on their current plan) for referring new SACCOs that achieve first M-Pesa subscription payment. Generate referral links from the org dashboard shareable via WhatsApp. Track funnel via PostHog (already in stack).

revenue_leakage.issue: No revenue from anonymized transit data products — the platform collects uniquely valuable GPS traces, trip patterns, passenger volumes, route adherence data, and compliance events that urban planners, government regulators, and researchers would pay for, but this data is entirely unmonetized
revenue_leakage.recommendation: Develop an anonymized transit data product for government planners, urban researchers, and regulators. A 'Transit Data API' or 'Analytics Export' subscription targeting PLANNER and REGULATOR roles at KES 20,000-50,000/month would create a high-margin B2G revenue stream with minimal marginal cost, leveraging DuckDB (already in stack) for aggregation queries.
